properties.decision:
A test written from the requirement and a test written to match the code are indistinguishable in the graph — and this repo records the difference in PROSE

*Anthony, 2026-08-03, on test-driven design: "Developing tests as you design is extremely important. It shapes system architecture, forces clear thinking about edge cases early, and prevents the tight coupling that makes retrofitting tests painful." His named risk is the one that bites here: "Confirmation bias: Testing code you already wrote proves what it does, not necessarily what it should do."* MEASURED: Verification carries criteria, kind, last_run_at, level, method, name, status — no field for when the check was authored, and none for whether it preceded the code. Yet 7 of reflow2's 105 verifications assert in their NAME that the test came first (ver:constructors-preserve: *"WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: all 6 defect cases failed and all 3 counterweights passed"*), two of them written on 2026-08-03. So the repo already practises test-first, already records it, and records it where NO COMPUTATION CAN READ IT — [BL-143]'s shape (an opinion smuggled in as data) and dec:edge-orthogonality's, from a new direction. The consequence is precise: a passing check written from the requirement and a passing check written to match the implementation are the same node, same status, same everything. reflow2 asserts dec:passing-is-verified — *verified means a check that passes* — while being unable to say what the check was evidence of. THE GUARD RAIL IS ANTHONY'S OWN CAVEAT — *"may not apply to or be feasible for all project types."* The adopt skill exists entirely for systems that already ship, where every recovered test is necessarily after the fact; a reading that scored that as failure would repeat exactly [BL-179]'s punish-correct-work trap. So: record the fact, report the signal, never grade it. Fix shape, and it pairs with [BL-143]'s already-decided criterion field on the same node type — one schema touch rather than two, which matters because a schema change pulls in the minor bump, the upgrade doc and the foundation-migration checklist. Candidates: an optional authored_at (order derivable against the Artifact's own dates), or an explicit provenance-of-evidence enum saying whether the check was written from the intent or from the implementation. Deciding which is the row. Size M

Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-185 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M.

UNANSWERED. Migrated as a `proposed` Decision because the row states a fork rather than a defect or a need: nobody has chosen, and recording it as intent would assert an answer.
